entries.663bed4d0f4dce18: Module drug discovery uses active substances of anticancer drugs that are already marketed as pharmaceuticals, combined together; because of this, almost no basic exploratory research is required, and clinical trials can begin 1 to 2 years after the work starts. Its strengths are that clinical efficacy and safety are easier to predict, that development takes less time than typical anticancer drug development, and that development risk is low. A further feature is that combinations of drugs whose patent terms have expired can still be patented as new anticancer drugs.

entries.8bbeedbe5bdb7315: This is an anticancer drug candidate compound targeting relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia. By continuous infusion at a low dose over a long period, it self-cleaves DNA strands and induces cancer cell death. Its Phase 3 clinical trial in the United States was discontinued following a recommendation from the independent safety committee (DSMB), while a Phase 1/2 clinical trial of combination therapy with venetoclax is progressing in the United States, and in Japan Nippon Shinyaku is conducting a Phase 1 clinical trial.

entries.ed75b748f575bd78: Delta-Fly Pharma, Inc. is an anticancer drug research and development company headquartered in Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture, with a Tokyo office in Chuo-ku, Tokyo. It has no subsidiaries, and the number of employees was 12 as of March 31, 2026. It does not have its own research laboratories or manufacturing facilities; it specializes in managing research and development, and uses external contract companies for manufacturing and testing work.

entries.f42122c7e503d797: This is a development candidate in which a polymer (4-arm-PEG) is bound to DFP-10917 to deliver it selectively to cancer tissue. Targeting solid tumors such as pancreatic cancer, it is conducting an expansion study of a Phase 1 clinical trial in the United States. It has entered into a joint development agreement with Sanyo Chemical Industries.
